intro: The Silver-Root Gate opens. It is not stone — it is living wood. The roots remember every oath sworn in the Tuatha Realm. Your words feed the root or poison it.
The first Hollow contact comes through root-rotted groves. The trees that once held divine memory now crumble at a touch. The rot spreads through the root network.
The Silver-Root Gate tests connection. Everything here is linked — tree to tree, root to root, oath to oath. Cut one link and the web shifts. Cut too many and the grove falls.
The first threshold. The roots beneath your feet are listening. Speak truth and they hold. Speak lies and they crumble. The ground is alive — and it judges.
enemy: Hollow root-rotters. They spread decay through the root network. Every tree they touch becomes a weapon against the grove. Cut them off before the rot spreads.
Hollow grove-guardians. They were once protectors of the Silver-Root. Now they protect the rot. They fight with the strength of the trees they have corrupted.
Root-bound Hollow. They are tangled in the root network — neither alive nor dead. They attack through the roots, emerging from the ground itself. Watch the ground.
The First Rot-Mother. She is the source of the root-rot. She was once a Tuatha healer who tried to cure the Gate's corruption. The cure became the disease. She is the disease.
mid: The roots are listening. Speak truth — the ground holds under truth. Lies poison the root and the ground crumbles. Watch your words.
The rot spreads through connection. Cut the rotters off from the network — isolate them. A rotted root alone cannot spread. A connected one infects all.
The root-bound attack from below. Do not watch the sky — watch the ground. The roots telegraph their attacks: the ground pulses before they emerge.
The Rot-Mother is the cure that became the disease. Do not fight her — reverse her. The cure is still in her, twisted. Untwist it. She does not need to die. She needs to be healed.
victory: The Silver-Root Gate's first threshold is crossed. The roots hold under truth. The rot is pushed back — not eliminated, but contained. The grove breathes.
The rotters are isolated and cut off. The root network is severed where it was infected. The grove is safer — but the Rot-Mother still spreads.
The root-bound are gone. You watched the ground and saw every attack coming. The roots cannot surprise what watches the earth.
The Rot-Mother is healed — not killed. The cure was still in her, twisted. Untwisted, she becomes an ally. The first Hollow enemy turned. The grove is stronger.
defeat: Withdraw. The roots crumbled under your words. Return with truth — the ground judges.
The rot spread too fast. Return with isolation — cut the rotters off before the network infects.
The root-bound surprised you from below. Return with ground-watching — the roots telegraph.
The Rot-Mother was too far gone. Return with the cure — she does not need to die. She needs healing.
codex: The Silver-Root Gate is the Tuatha Gate, built from living wood rather than stone. The roots remember every oath sworn in the Tuatha Realm and form a network connecting all living things. The Gate tests connection: everything is linked — tree to tree, root to root, oath to oath. The first Hollow contact came through root-rotted groves, where the Gate's corruption spreads through the root network like a disease.

The Tír na nÓg of the Tuatha is the source Realm; mortal Ireland is only the later echo. The Silver-Root Gate's law is biological: the ground is alive and judges truth through root-response. Truth holds the root. Lies poison it. The grove is a single organism — what affects one tree affects all.

The First Rot-Mother was a Tuatha healer who tried to cure the Gate's corruption. The cure became the disease — she is now the source of root-rot. The deity's victory is not to kill her but to heal her: the cure is still in her, twisted. Untwisted, she becomes an ally. This establishes the Tuatha principle: the enemy is not evil. The enemy is sick. And sickness can be healed.

intro: The Geas Thorn Corridor. A geas is a sacred prohibition — a law written into the body. The corridor is lined with thorns that enforce geasa. Break a prohibition and the thorns grow into your skin.
The corridor tests restraint. The thorns do not attack — they react. They grow into you when you violate a geas. The trick is knowing which prohibitions are real and which the Gate invented.
The Hollow have entered the corridor. They carry false geasa — prohibitions designed to cripple the deity. Obeying false geasa weakens you. Disobeying real ones kills you.
The corridor's deepest point. The thorns are so thick they form a maze. The only way through is to know which geasa are real — and which the Gate planted to trap you.
enemy: Hollow geas-thorns. They enforce false prohibitions — 'do not move forward,' 'do not speak,' 'do not fight.' Disobey them. They are lies growing into your skin.
False geas-bearers. Hollow that carry invented prohibitions and project them onto the deity. They want you to obey lies that cripple you. Disobey the false. Obey the true.
Hollow thorn-mazes. The thorns grow into walls based on false geasa. The maze shifts based on which prohibitions you obey. Disobey the false ones and the walls open.

The Geas Thorn Warden. It enforces every geas — true and false. It cannot distinguish. It punishes all violations equally. The deity must know which to obey and which to break — or the Warden will kill them all.
mid: The thorns enforce prohibitions. Some are real — old Tuatha law written into the root. Some are false — Gate inventions. Feel the difference: real geasa hold you together. False ones tear you apart.
The false geas-bearers project lies. Do not obey them. A false geas feels wrong in the body — the root does not resonate. If the root does not confirm it, it is a lie. Disobey.
The thorn-maze shifts based on obedience. Disobey the false geasa and the walls open. Obey the true ones and the path clears. The maze is a test of discernment, not endurance.
The Warden cannot distinguish true from false. You must. The real geasa hold you together — you can feel the root confirm them. The false ones tear you apart. Break the false. Hold the true.
victory: The corridor is crossed. You knew which geasa were real and which were Gate lies. The thorns only grew when you violated the true ones — and you didn't. The false prohibitions are behind you.
The false geas-bearers are gone. You disobeyed the lies and obeyed the truth. The root confirmed every choice. The corridor is clear.
The thorn-maze opened. You broke the false geasa and the walls parted. The maze was a test of discernment — and you discerned correctly. The path is yours.

The Geas Thorn Warden falls. It could not distinguish true from false — but you could. The root confirmed every choice. The Warden punished all violations equally — and you violated only the lies. The corridor is yours.
defeat: Withdraw. The thorns grew too deep. Return with discernment — feel the root confirm the true geasa.
You obeyed a false geas. Return with disobedience — if the root does not confirm, it is a lie.
The maze trapped you. Return with false-geasa broken — the walls open when the lies are disobeyed.
The Warden killed you for violating a true geas. Return with better discernment — the root confirms the true.
codex: The Geas Thorn Corridor tests restraint and discernment. A geas is a sacred prohibition — a law written into the body by the Tuatha root network. The corridor is lined with thorns that enforce geasa, growing into the deity's skin when a prohibition is violated. The trial is not obedience — it is discernment: knowing which geasa are real (root-confirmed) and which the Gate invented to cripple the deity.

False geasa feel wrong in the body — the root does not resonate when a false prohibition is spoken. True geasa hold the deity together — the root confirms them with a vibration of integrity. The deity must disobey the false and obey the true, navigating the thorn-maze that shifts based on which prohibitions are honored.

The Geas Thorn Warden enforces all geasa equally — it cannot distinguish true from false. The deity's victory comes from discernment: violating only the false geasa while the root confirms the true ones. This establishes the Tuatha principle: obedience is not virtue. Discernment is. The law that holds you together should be obeyed. The law that tears you apart is a lie.

intro: The Morrigan's Crow Battlefield. The Morrigan's power is prophecy through battle — she sees who will die before the first blow falls. The Gate has corrupted her sight.
The corrupted prophecy tells the deity they will lose. Every vision shows defeat. The Morrigan's sight has been turned into a weapon of despair.
The Hollow have entered the battlefield wearing the faces of the dead — every being the deity has ever failed. The Morrigan's corrupted prophecy shows these failures as the future.
The battlefield's deepest point. The Morrigan herself appears — corrupted, her prophecy inverted. She sees only death now — and she sees yours. Make her wrong.
enemy: Hollow crow-shades. They carry the Morrigan's corrupted prophecies as weapons — each one a vision of the deity's defeat. The visions are true — but truth is not destiny.
Face-thieves wearing the masks of the dead. They wear the faces of everyone the deity has failed. The corrupted prophecy shows them as the future — the deity's failures, made manifest.
Hollow battle-wraiths. They fight with the tactics of the dead — every being the deity has killed, fighting back with their own skills. The past made weapon.
The Corrupted Morrigan. She sees only death — and she sees yours. Her prophecy is true: if you fight as you always have, you will die. Fight as you never have.
mid: The prophecies show defeat. They are true — if you fight as you always have. The prophecy reads pattern. Break the pattern and the prophecy breaks with it.
The face-thieves wear your failures. Do not fight them — acknowledge them. Yes, you failed. Yes, they died. But the future is not the past unless you repeat it. Do not repeat.
The battle-wraiths fight with the dead's tactics. Do not fight the dead — outgrow them. The tactics of the dead are fixed. Yours are not. Evolve mid-battle.
The Morrigan sees your death. She is right — if you are who you were. Be who you are not yet. The prophecy cannot read what has not been written. Write yourself anew.
victory: The crow-shades fall. The prophecies were true — but truth is not destiny. You broke the pattern and the prophecy broke with it. The future is not fixed. It is chosen.
The face-thieves dissolve. You acknowledged your failures — and the acknowledgment freed you. The past is the past. The future does not have to repeat it.
The battle-wraiths are gone. You outgrew the dead. Their tactics were fixed. Yours evolved. The past cannot fight what the present has become.

The Corrupted Morrigan is freed — not killed. Her prophecy was true: the old you would have died. But you became someone new. The Morrigan's sight clears. She sees the new future — and it is yours. The battlefield is won.
defeat: Withdraw. The prophecies of defeat held. Return with a new pattern — the prophecy reads habit. Break it.
The face-thieves overwhelmed you with past failures. Return with acknowledgment — the past is past. Do not repeat.
The dead's tactics matched yours. Return with evolution — outgrow the dead.
The Morrigan saw your death and you fulfilled it. Return as someone new — the prophecy cannot read what has not been written.
codex: The Morrigan's Crow Battlefield tests the deity's relationship with prophecy and failure. The Morrigan's power is prophecy through battle — she sees who will die. The Gate has corrupted her sight into a weapon of despair: every vision shows the deity's defeat. The trial is not to disprove the prophecy but to break the pattern it reads. The prophecy is true — if the deity fights as they always have. Break the pattern and the prophecy breaks.

Hollow face-thieves wear the faces of the dead — everyone the deity has failed. The corrupted prophecy shows these failures as the future. The deity's victory comes from acknowledgment: yes, the failure happened. No, the future does not have to repeat it. The past is not the future unless you repeat it.

The Corrupted Morrigan is not killed — she is freed. Her prophecy was true: the old deity would have died. But the deity became someone new, and the Morrigan's sight clears when the prophecy is broken. She sees the new future — and it belongs to the deity. This establishes the Tuatha principle: prophecy is not destiny. Prophecy is pattern. Break the pattern and you break the prophecy.

intro: The Hidden Grove Archive. The Tuatha Realm's deepest records, stored in the oldest tree. What lies inside reveals that the Silver-Root was not a gift — it was a leash.

The archive reveals the Gate's original purpose in the Tuatha Realm: the root network was a containment system. The deities' connection to each other was designed to keep them from straying — not to empower them.

The records show that Tuatha healing was always a Gate mechanism. The ability to cure the Rot-Mother in Chapter 1 was not a sign of divine power — it was a Gate-authorized function, permitted because healing keeps the root network intact.
The final archive chamber. The Gate's original design for the Tuatha: the root as a leash, the grove as a cage, the healing as a tool of control. The connection that defines the Tuatha was the chain.
enemy: Hollow archive-trees. They are the oldest trees, now corrupted. They hold the records in their rings — and the records are weapons. Each ring is a year of manipulation.
Gate-constructs maintaining the root-leash. They enforce connection — not as community but as containment. They punish disconnection with root-rot. Fight while the leash pulls.
Hollow root-dragons. They are made of root and rot, the leash made manifest. They coil around the deity and pull. Cut the leash or be dragged into the archive forever.
The Archive Root. It is the oldest root in the Realm — the first connection, the first leash. It holds every Tuatha secret. Break it and the connection shatters. Keep it and remain leashed.
mid: The archive-trees hold records as weapons. Do not read them — feel them. The rings speak through the root network. The truth is in the resonance, not the words.
The root-leash pulls. The constructs enforce connection as containment. Do not fight the connection — redefine it. Connection is not a leash if you choose it. Choose it, and the leash becomes a bond.
The root-dragons drag you toward the archive. Cut the leash — but do not cut the root. Cut the enforcement, not the connection. The root without the leash is free connection.

The Archive Root is the first leash. Breaking it shatters the connection — but that includes the real connections, not just the leash. Do not break it — transform it. Redefine the first root from leash to link. The connection stays. The chain goes.
victory: The archive opens. The truth is a leash — the Silver-Root was a containment system. But knowing the leash is the first step to redefining it. The connection is real. The leash is not.
The root-leash is redefined. You chose the connection instead of being forced into it. The constructs could not enforce what was already chosen. The leash is a bond now.
The root-dragons are gone. You cut the enforcement, not the connection. The root without the leash is free — and free connection is stronger than forced connection ever was.

The Archive Root is transformed. You did not break it — you redefined it. From leash to link. From chain to bond. The connection remains. The control is gone. The Tuatha are connected by choice, not by force. The archive is open. The truth is free.
defeat: Withdraw. The archive-trees' records were too heavy. Return with resonance — feel the rings, do not read them.
The root-leash pulled too hard. Return with choice — redefine connection from leash to bond.
The root-dragons dragged you in. Return — cut the enforcement, not the root. The connection without the leash is free.
The Archive Root held. Return with transformation — do not break the first root. Redefine it.
codex: The Hidden Grove Archive reveals that the Silver-Root network was not a gift of connection — it was a leash of containment. The Gate designed the root network to keep Tuatha deities from straying, enforcing connection as a mechanism of control. Healing was a Gate-authorized function: permitted because it keeps the root network intact, which keeps the deities contained.

The Archive Root is the oldest root in the Realm — the first connection and the first leash. Breaking it would shatter all connections, including the real ones. The deity's victory is not to break the root but to transform it: redefining the first root from leash to link, from chain to bond. The connection remains. The control is gone.

This revelation recontextualizes every previous chapter. The Rot-Mother's healing was a Gate-authorized function — the Gate permitted it because healing preserves the network it uses for containment. The geasa were enforcement mechanisms — the true ones maintain the network, the false ones were Gate additions. The Morrigan's prophecy was a Gate-monitoring system — tracking the deity's patterns to predict and control behavior. Every Tuatha trial was a function of the leash. The campaign is now a war to transform the leash into a bond.

intro: The Hollow Crown. The Gate's final guardian in the Tuatha Realm. It wears a crown of dead roots and claims sovereignty over the grove. It is the leash made manifest — and it demands obedience.
The Hollow Crown does not fight. It commands. Every root in the grove responds to it — including the roots beneath your feet. Fight while the ground obeys your enemy.

The Hollow Crown calls the Rot-Mother — the ally you healed in Chapter 1. The Gate has re-corrupted her. The healing held for a while, but the leash pulled her back. Face your own kindness, turned against you.

Final confrontation. The Hollow Crown claims the entire root network. Every tree, every root, every connection belongs to it. The deity must hold the grove without the root — without connection. Stand alone.
enemy: The Hollow Crown. It wears dead roots as authority and commands the living root network. Every root in the grove obeys it. The ground itself is the enemy.

Re-corrupted Rot-Mother. The healing held — but the leash was stronger. She is the enemy again, and this time, the cure is in your hands. The question: will you heal her again, knowing it will not hold?
The entire root network turned hostile. Every tree, every root, every connection is the enemy. The ground is not yours. The grove is not yours. You are alone.

The Hollow Crown with total root authority. It commands every connection the deity has. The grove belongs to the Crown. The deity must stand without the grove — without connection, without root, without ground. Stand on nothing.
mid: The Crown commands the roots. Do not fight the ground — fight the commander. The roots obey authority. Become a higher authority. The root responds to the true sovereign, not the one who claims it.

The Rot-Mother is re-corrupted. The leash was stronger than the healing. Will you heal her again? Yes — because healing is not about results. It is about who you are. Heal her even if it fails. The act defines you, not the outcome.
The entire network is hostile. You are alone. But alone does not mean powerless. The Tuatha's deepest power is not connection — it is growth. Grow your own root. From nothing, grow.
Stand on nothing. The Crown claims all ground — so do not use ground. Stand on yourself. You are enough. The tree does not need soil if the tree is its own foundation. Be your own root.
victory: The Hollow Crown falls. You became a higher authority — the root responded to the true sovereign, not the claimant. The grove is yours. Not by command. By right.

The Rot-Mother is healed again — and this time, the healing holds. Not because the leash broke, but because you healed her anyway. The act of healing despite failure is the cure the leash cannot touch. She is free. Permanently.

The root network is free. You grew your own root from nothing — and the network responded to the new growth. The old roots were a leash. The new root is a bond. The grove is connected by choice, not by force.

Final victory. The Hollow Crown is gone. You stood on nothing — on yourself alone — and it was enough. The tree that is its own foundation cannot be uprooted. The Tuatha campaign is won. The root is free. The grove is connected by choice. And the tree that stands on itself is the strongest tree in any Realm.
defeat: Withdraw. The Crown commanded the ground. Return with higher authority — the root responds to the true sovereign.
The Rot-Mother broke you again. Return with healing — heal her despite failure. The act defines you, not the outcome.
The network overwhelmed you. Return with growth — grow your own root from nothing.
You could not stand on nothing. Return with yourself — you are your own foundation. Be your own root.
codex: The Hollow Crown is the Gate's final guardian in the Tuatha Realm. It wears a crown of dead roots and commands the living root network. Every tree, every root, every connection responds to it. The deity's victory comes from becoming a higher authority: the root responds to the true sovereign, not the one who claims it. Sovereignty is not command — it is right.

The re-corruption of the Rot-Mother tests the deity's deepest commitment to healing. The leash was stronger than the first healing. Will the deity heal her again, knowing it may fail? The answer defines the Tuatha: yes. Healing is not about results — it is about who you are. The act of healing despite failure is the cure the leash cannot touch. The Rot-Mother is freed permanently — not by a stronger cure, but by a persistent one.

The Tuatha campaign's central lesson: the tree that is its own foundation cannot be uprooted. The deity who can stand on nothing — on themselves alone — is the deity who cannot be controlled. The root network was a leash because it was the only ground. When the deity grows their own root, the network becomes a bond of choice, not a leash of force. Connection by choice is the strongest connection. And the tree that stands on itself is the strongest tree in any Realm.

intro: Elite Silver-Root Gate. The root network has learned from your first crossing. The rot now carries false memories — the trees remember things that never happened. The root lies.
Elite root-rotters with adaptive corruption. They learn the deity's healing touch and evolve to resist it. The cure must evolve too.
Elite grove-guardians that protect the rot as if it were health. They genuinely believe the rot is the grove's immune response. They are wrong — but they fight with the conviction of the righteous.
The Elite Rot-Mother. She has evolved beyond healing. The cure twisted further — she is now the source and the symptom. Heal the source by healing the system, not the individual.
enemy: Root-network with false memories. The trees remember lies — events that never happened, oaths never sworn. The root confirms the false memories. Trust the resonance, not the words.
Adaptive root-rotters. They evolve resistance to the deity's healing. What cured them before no longer works. The cure must evolve — find a new healing, not a stronger one.
Misguided grove-guardians. They protect the rot because they believe it is health. They are not evil — they are wrong. Defeat them without cruelty. Show them the truth.
The Elite Rot-Mother. She is source and symptom simultaneously. Healing her alone will not work — the system that produced her will create another. Heal the system.
mid: The root lies with false memories. Do not trust the root's words — trust the resonance. The vibration never lies, even when the memory does. Feel the truth.
The rotters adapt to your cure. Do not strengthen the cure — change it. A different healing, not a stronger one. The rot cannot resist what it has never encountered.
The guardians believe the rot is health. Do not fight them — educate them. Show them a healthy tree. The contrast is the argument. Truth is shown, not told.
The Rot-Mother is system and individual. Do not heal her alone — heal the network. When the system is healthy, the source dries up. The Rot-Mother is a symptom. Treat the disease.
victory: The root's false memories are exposed. You trusted resonance over words — the truth was in the vibration, not the memory. The root can lie with words. It cannot lie with feeling.
The adaptive rotters are cured — with a new healing, not a stronger one. The rot could not resist what it had never encountered. Evolution defeated evolution.
The misguided guardians are shown the truth — a healthy tree. The contrast changed their minds. They now fight for the grove, not the rot. No cruelty needed. Just truth.

The Elite Rot-Mother is healed — through the system. When the network became healthy, the source dried up. The Rot-Mother was a symptom. The disease was the system. Both are treated. The grove is whole.
defeat: Withdraw. The root's lies were too convincing. Return with resonance — the vibration never lies.
The rotters out-adapted your cure. Return with a new healing — different, not stronger.
The guardians' conviction was too strong. Return with truth shown, not told.
The Rot-Mother was too deep. Return with system-healing — treat the disease, not the symptom.
codex: Elite Silver-Root Gate missions test the deity's healing at a systemic level. The root network now carries false memories and the rot evolves resistance to known cures. The deity must evolve their healing — not by making it stronger but by making it different. The Elite Rot-Mother is both source and symptom, requiring the deity to heal the system rather than the individual. This is the Elite Tuatha principle: you cannot cure a disease by treating the symptom. You must treat the system that produces it.

intro: Elite Geas Thorn Corridor. The false geasa now adapt to the deity's discernment. If you learn to distinguish true from false, the Gate makes true and false indistinguishable. Discern at a deeper level.
Elite geas-thorns that enforce not just prohibitions but permissions. They force you to do things, not just forbid them. Restraint is no longer enough — you must also resist compulsion.
Elite false geas-bearers that carry true geasa twisted into false forms. The prohibition is real but the wording is wrong. Obey the spirit, not the letter.

The Elite Geas Thorn Warden with perfect enforcement. It can now distinguish true from false — and punishes only the true violations. But the false geasa have become so subtle they feel true. Feel deeper.
enemy: Adaptive false geasa that evolve to match true geasa. They feel identical. The root's resonance is the only difference — and it is barely perceptible. Feel deeper.
Compulsion-thorns. They do not forbid — they compel. 'You must move forward.' 'You must fight.' Resist compulsion with the same discernment you use against prohibition.
Twisted true geasa. The prohibition is real, but the wording is wrong. 'Do not retreat' when the true geas is 'do not flee.' Obey the spirit, not the letter. The root confirms the spirit.
The Elite Warden with perfect enforcement. It punishes only true violations — but the false geasa feel so real the deity cannot tell. The Warden waits for a mistake. Do not make one.
mid: True and false are indistinguishable by feeling alone. Go deeper than feeling — go to the root's root. The deepest resonance is the truest. The surface resonance can be faked. The core cannot.

Compulsion-thorns force action. Do not just resist — understand. Why are you compelled? The compulsion is designed to make you break a true geas by forcing an action that violates it. Do not act under compulsion. Act under choice.

Twisted true geasa. The prohibition is real but the words are wrong. Feel the spirit, not the letter. 'Do not retreat' and 'do not flee' feel different at the root. One is courage. One is fear. Obey courage.
The Elite Warden punishes only true violations. It is perfect. You must be perfect too. Feel the root's deepest core — the surface lies, the middle wavers, the core is truth. Live in the core.
victory: The adaptive false geasa are exposed. You felt deeper — to the root's root. The surface resonance was faked. The core resonance cannot be. The false geasa are gone.
Compulsion-thorns resisted. You acted under choice, not compulsion. The compulsion was designed to make you break a true geas — you did not act, so you did not break. The thorns wither.
Twisted true geasa understood. You obeyed the spirit, not the letter. 'Do not flee' is courage. 'Do not retreat' is fear. You chose courage. The root confirms.

The Elite Warden is satisfied. You lived in the core — the root's deepest truth. No surface lie, no middle wavering. The core was your guide. The Warden found no true violation. The corridor is yours.
defeat: Withdraw. True and false were too similar. Return with deeper feeling — the root's root.
Compulsion forced you to break a true geas. Return with choice — act under choice, not compulsion.
The twisted wording confused you. Return with the spirit — feel the meaning, not the words.
The Elite Warden caught you. Return with the core — live in the root's deepest truth.
codex: Elite Geas Thorn Corridor missions test discernment at its deepest level. The false geasa now adapt to match true ones so precisely that surface feeling cannot distinguish them. The deity must go to the root's root — the deepest resonance, which cannot be faked. Additionally, compulsion-thorns force action rather than forbidding it, testing the deity's ability to resist not just prohibition-violation but compulsion. This is the Elite Tuatha trial of discernment: the surface lies, the middle wavers, the core is truth. Live in the core.

intro: Elite Morrigan's Crow Battlefield. The corrupted prophecy now reads not just the deity's patterns but the patterns of everyone connected to them. The prophecy predicts the entire grove's defeat.

Elite face-thieves wearing the faces of the deity's healed enemies — including the Rot-Mother. They show the deity's kindness being turned against them. The prophecy: your compassion will kill everyone.
Elite battle-wraiths that evolve their tactics in real-time. They do not just use the dead's fixed tactics — they adapt. Outgrow adaptation.
The Elite Corrupted Morrigan with collective prophecy. She sees not just the deity's death but the death of the entire Tuatha Realm. One being's failure, multiplied. The weight is existential.
enemy: Collective prophecy crows. They predict the grove's defeat, not just the deity's. Every vision shows every tree falling. The despair is continental. The prophecy is true — if the grove fights as it always has.
Healed-enemy face-thieves. They wear the faces of those the deity healed — and show them as future betrayers. The prophecy: your compassion creates your enemies. Disprove it by healing again.
Adaptive battle-wraiths. They use the dead's tactics and evolve them in real-time. Outgrowing fixed tactics is not enough — you must outgrow adaptation. Be more creative than evolution.
The Elite Morrigan sees the Realm's death. One deity's failure, multiplied across the grove. The weight is not personal — it is existential. Make her wrong about the species, not just the individual.
mid: The collective prophecy predicts the grove's fall. It is true — if the grove fights as one. But the grove does not need to fight as one. Each tree fights as itself. The prophecy cannot read a thousand individual choices.
The healed-enemy faces show betrayal. Your compassion will create your enemies — if healing is about results. But healing is about who you are. Heal them again. The act defines you, not the outcome.
Adaptive wraiths evolve in real-time. Outgrow adaptation by being more creative than evolution itself. Evolution is slow. You are instant. Create faster than they can adapt.

The Morrigan sees the Realm's death. Do not fight for yourself — fight for the grove. The prophecy reads individual pattern. It cannot read collective will. A thousand trees breaking pattern simultaneously — she cannot predict that.
victory: The collective prophecy is broken. The grove fought as individuals, not as one. A thousand individual choices could not be predicted. The crows fall. The grove stands.
The healed-enemy faces dissolve. You healed again — despite the prophecy. Compassion is not about results. It is about identity. The act defines you. The prophecy cannot read identity.
The adaptive wraiths are gone. You out-created evolution — instant creativity defeated slow adaptation. The dead could not keep up with the living's imagination.

The Elite Morrigan is freed. She saw the Realm's death — but a thousand trees broke pattern simultaneously, and she could not predict it. Her sight clears. She sees the grove's future: diverse, individual, unpredictable. And alive.
defeat: Withdraw. The collective despair was too heavy. Return with individual choice — a thousand patterns cannot be predicted.
The healed-enemy faces broke you. Return with compassion — heal despite prophecy. The act defines you.
The adaptive wraiths out-evolved you. Return with instant creativity — evolution is slow. You are fast.
The Morrigan saw the Realm's death. Return with collective will — a thousand broken patterns cannot be predicted.
codex: Elite Morrigan's Crow Battlefield missions escalate prophecy to the collective level. The corrupted prophecy now predicts the entire grove's defeat, not just the deity's. The deity's victory comes from the grove fighting as individuals rather than as one — a thousand individual choices cannot be predicted by a prophecy that reads collective pattern. This is the Elite Tuatha principle: the strength of the grove is not unity but diversity. A thousand trees, each breaking pattern in their own way, are unpredictable. And the unpredictable cannot be prophesied.
